title: pdf_prebake header documents a priv-dir CLI argument that main() never reads
detail: The usage comment promises an accepted argument and a default; main() hardcodes "priv" and never touches argv. The documented command works only by accident of cwd, and the documented behavior does not exist.
recommended_fix: Either parse the argument in main() (e.g. via argv) with the documented default, or delete the argument from the usage comment.

title: str_opt helper, gleam/result, and three sql row-type imports are never used
detail: str_opt is defined but never called anywhere in the file; gleam/result has no call site; GetCoApplicantsByApplicationRow/GetDocumentsByApplicationRow/GetIncomeSourcesByApplicationRow appear only in the import (snapshot fields are bare [] literals). Dead code in a new module.
recommended_fix: Delete str_opt, the gleam/result import, and the three unused type imports; or actually populate the snapshot lists using those row types.

title: Demo network lint greps two tokens; a demo module importing client/src/api/ modules evades it
evidence: + VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rn "rsvp\|api_helpers" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true) ... and in the same diff the mock states the seam: "The client is a Lustre SPA with a clean client/src/api/ seam." ... success message: "Demo mode is fully client-side: no API/network imports in demo/."
detail: The guard matches only the literal strings rsvp/api_helpers and gleam/fetch. An `import api/...` of the real API layer in a demo module passes the lint while the step claims no API imports. It also matches comments/strings, inviting false positives.
recommended_fix: Grep for '^import (api/|rsvp|gleam/fetch|gleam/http)' anchored to import statements, keeping the demo_api.gleam fetch exclusion.

title: Sara Walsh flag claims rent is 31% of stated income; the fixture's own numbers give 72%
evidence:
flags: "[{\"label\":\"Rent sits at 31% of stated income — borderline\",\"severity\":\"amber\",\"category\":\"income_affordability\"}...",
      insight: "Affordability is borderline at 31% of stated income. ...",
      row: simple_row(
        "a-sara",
        ...
        340_000,
        340_000,
... and monthly_rent_cents: 245_000,
detail: Rent €2,450 against income €3,400 is 72%, not 31%. The same file asserts the fixtures mirror the client stories; a landlord running the mental math sees a demo that cannot do its own arithmetic.
recommended_fix: Recompute the ratio from monthly_rent_cents and the row income and fix the flag and insight text (or change the income figure).

title: pdf_prebake main() reports failures but always exits 0
evidence:
_ ->
      io.println(
        "FAILED: "
        <> int_to_string(failures)
        <> " of "
        <> int_to_string(list.length(results))
        <> " PDFs failed",
      )
detail: On any generate/write failure the tool prints FAILED and returns success. Any scripted regeneration (the documented gleam run command) cannot detect that PDFs are missing or stale.
recommended_fix: Halt with a non-zero exit code when failures > 0 (e.g. erlang halt(1) via existing Erlang FFI conventions).

title: Marta's category_scores JSON omits rental_history present in all seven other payloads
detail: Every other payload carries six category keys including rental_history; Marta has five. If deliberate (first-time-renter story) it is undocumented; if the Typst template iterates a fixed key set, her PDF renders a missing/different category row.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit rental_history value (or null with template handling) and a comment stating the divergence is intentional.

title: Employer reference Rachel O'Brien is given the email roberts@finlaydigital.example.com
evidence:
employer_ref_name: Some("Rachel O'Brien"),
    employer_ref_phone: Some("01 555 0188"),
    employer_ref_email: Some("roberts@finlaydigital.example.com"),
detail: The reference's name and email local-part belong to different people. The mock document itself declares 'the fixtures ARE the product marketing'; this is the kind of detail a prospect notices in the showpiece report.
